faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Virginia Beach?
faqs.a: It depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing and cleanup the job needs. Our crew inspects first, shows you the entry points we found in Virginia Beach, and gives you a quote after inspection before any removal or sealing work begins — no prices promised over the phone.

faqs.q: A snake turned up at my Virginia Beach home — what happens next?
faqs.a: Call us and keep people and pets clear until we identify it. Most Virginia Beach snake calls are harmless rat snakes, racers, or garter snakes, and the eastern copperhead — venomous and found statewide — is the one to treat with real caution. Snakes are the one class Virginia allows a permit holder to move a short distance: same or neighboring county or city, suitable habitat, with the release-site landowner's written permission, and we report the move to DWR. We never kill a snake as a marketed service.

Virginia Beach.wildlife_intro:
Virginia Beach runs from dense oceanfront and bay neighborhoods to Sandbridge and Princess Anne farmland, so one city holds rat, raccoon, snake, and bat work of very different kinds in Virginia Beach. Our crew's calls here follow the ground: atlantic oceanfront and Chesapeake Bay shore, Back Bay and First Landing State Park woods, Lynnhaven River inlets. Raccoons and gray squirrels take attics and chimneys, striped skunks and opossums work yards and crawlspaces, and bats settle older rooflines in summer.

In spring we remove denning raccoon and squirrel families before the young are mobile. Summer brings skunk, groundhog, and snake calls and the bat maternity season, when exclusion waits under Virginia permit conditions. Fall is sealing season in Virginia Beach — squirrels, rats, and bats all test the same gaps looking for winter shelter, and our crew closes them after the animals are out, because sealing alone rarely holds.
